school_name: Columbia University in the City of New York
title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
description: Discover the functional student spaces and specialized facilities that define daily life at Columbia, from hidden library stacks to rooftop observatories.

cards.title: The Butler Stacks
cards.subtitle: Deep-core study carrels in Butler Library
cards.notes: Enter through the 3rd-floor circulation desk to find these windowless, multi-level carrels. It is the ultimate destination for distraction-free, silent cramming sessions.
cards.short_summary: A multi-level labyrinth of silent study carrels located in the central core of Columbia's main humanities library.
cards.evidence_claim: Butler Library's main collection of 2 million volumes is located in the Stacks, which feature study tables and wireless access throughout.
cards.access_notes: Open 24/7 during the academic term for CUID holders; accessible via the 3rd-floor entrance.

cards.title: Avery Lower Level
cards.subtitle: Quiet basement study area in Avery Hall
cards.notes: Head to the lower floor for a cozy, ultra-quiet atmosphere surrounded by architectural archives. It is often less crowded than the main reading room upstairs.
cards.short_summary: A serene, subterranean study space within the world-renowned Avery Architectural & Fine Arts Library.
cards.evidence_claim: Avery Library offers quiet study spaces on its lower floor, which are available to all students space-permitting.
cards.access_notes: Open until 11:00 PM most weeknights; CUID required for entry.

cards.title: Pupin Rooftop Observatory
cards.subtitle: Stargazing dome atop Pupin Hall
cards.notes: Visit on select Friday nights for free public lectures and guided stargazing through the 14-inch telescope. It offers a rare clear view of the sky from Manhattan.
cards.short_summary: A historic rooftop observatory atop Pupin Hall that hosts public stargazing events and astronomy lectures.
cards.evidence_claim: The astronomy department offers free public lectures and guided stargazing at the Rutherfurd Observatory every other Friday during the school year.
cards.access_notes: Public events typically start at 8:00 PM on Fridays; check the outreach calendar for specific dates.

cards.title: Lerner Piano Lounge
cards.subtitle: Student lounge in Alfred J. Lerner Hall
cards.notes: Relax in the 2nd-floor lounge where students often play the Steinway Grand Piano. It's a popular spot for casual socializing between classes.
cards.short_summary: A comfortable central lounge in the student union featuring a grand piano available for student use.
cards.evidence_claim: The Main Lounge in Lerner Hall features a Steinway Grand Piano that students are welcome to play.
cards.source_title: Main Lounge | Alfred J. Lerner Hall
cards.access_notes: Accessible during Lerner Hall building hours; open to all CUID holders.

cards.title: St. Paul's Chapel
cards.subtitle: Historic non-denominational chapel
cards.notes: Step inside to experience the incredible acoustics and the Nakashima Peace Altar. It is a designated quiet space for meditation and prayer daily.
cards.short_summary: A landmarked campus chapel known for its Byzantine-style interior and exceptional acoustic properties.
cards.evidence_claim: The chapel is open daily for private meditation and prayer, Monday to Friday, 10am to 5pm.
cards.access_notes: Open Monday-Friday, 10:00 AM to 5:00 PM for meditation; also hosts evening concerts.

cards.title: NoCo Science Library
cards.subtitle: Modern study space in the Northwest Corner Building
cards.notes: Utilize the floor-to-ceiling windows for a bright study environment. The 400 level allows for collaborative work, while the 600 level is for quiet study.
cards.short_summary: A high-tech, light-filled library focusing on STEM fields with designated collaborative and quiet zones.
cards.evidence_claim: The Science & Engineering Library features collaborative spaces on the 400 level and quiet study on the 600 level.
cards.access_notes: CUID required; hours vary by semester but typically open until midnight.

cards.title: Philosophy Hall Lounge
cards.subtitle: GSAS student center in Philosophy Hall
cards.notes: Located in Room 301, this lounge offers a quiet community space for graduate students. It features an acoustic design to minimize background noise.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated social and study hub for graduate students located in the historic Philosophy Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: The Graduate Student Center in 301 Philosophy Hall offers a community space for graduate students to socialize and study.
cards.access_notes: Open daily 8:00 AM to 12:00 midnight; CUID access required.

cards.title: Earl Hall Prayer Space
cards.subtitle: Multi-faith prayer and meditation rooms
cards.notes: Visit Room 110 for a dedicated prayer space with rugs. The building serves as a sanctuary for spiritual well-being and student religious life.
cards.short_summary: A historic building housing multi-faith prayer rooms and the Office of Religious Life.
cards.evidence_claim: Earl Hall Room 110 provides a dedicated prayer space for the Columbia community.
cards.access_notes: Accessible during building hours; open to all students for reflection and prayer.

cards.entity_name: Milstein Center for Teaching and Learning
cards.title: Milstein Reading Nooks
cards.subtitle: Modern study alcoves at Barnard College
cards.notes: Look for the signature green swiveling chairs and blue booth-style couches on the 2nd floor. These nooks offer great views and integrated power outlets.
cards.short_summary: Highly sought-after individual study alcoves and modern seating in Barnard's flagship library.
cards.evidence_claim: The Milstein Center features individual desk nooks and booth-style couches on the second floor for focused studying.
cards.access_notes: Open to Columbia and Barnard students; volume decreases as you ascend to higher floors.

cards.title: Gottesman Silent Floor
cards.subtitle: Quiet study at Teachers College
cards.notes: Head to the 3rd floor of Russell Hall for intensive, silent study. The large windows provide scenic views of the surrounding Morningside Heights neighborhood.
cards.short_summary: The designated silent floor of the largest education library in the United States.
cards.evidence_claim: The 3rd floor of the Gottesman Libraries is a designated quiet space for intensive study.
cards.access_notes: Open to TC and Columbia affiliates; check library site for current seasonal hours.
